items.title: Custom header field not available in Mass Changes to Purchase Contracts app

items.text:
Hi Experts, 
 I’m working on an SAP S/4HANA Cloud (Public Edition) project. My client wants to update a custom field on purchase contracts in bulk using the Mass Changes to Purchase Contracts functionality. I’m not able to get the field to show up there, and I’d appreciate your guidance. 
 What I’ve done so far 
 Created a custom field in the Custom Fields app with these details: 
 Field Label: Contract Engineer 
 Identifier: YY1_ContractEngineer 
 Field Type: Text (12) 
 Business Context: Procurement: Purchasing Document (MM_PURDOC_HEADER) 
 Published the field successfully (status shows Published ).

 Are there restrictions on which custom field types or lengths can be updated through mass changes? 
 Is there any additional step required after publishing, such as a refresh of the app, a wait for the extension to be activated, or a user role/authorization adjustment? 
 Has anyone successfully enabled a custom field in the Mass Changes to Purchase Contracts app and can share the steps? 
 System details 
 SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition (release: add your release, e.g. 2508) 
 App: Mass Changes to Purchase Contracts 
 Custom Fields app: field published, CDS views enabled 
 I’ve attached a screenshot of the Custom Fields app showing the User Interfaces tab with the enabled CDS views.

items.title: SAP SuccessFactors 2H 2026 Release: What’s New & What Matters
items.author: nageshpolu
items.text:
A reorganisation to plan. An employee document to find. A business rule to maintain. A failed integration to investigate. 
 These are the kinds of everyday tasks I look at when reviewing a SuccessFactors release. A feature becomes interesting when I can connect it to work that an HR team, manager or administrator actually needs to do. 
 In my 2H 2025 release review blog , I focused on the foundations. My 1H 2026 review followed the progress in governance, skills and connected processes. 
 For 2H 2026, my shortlist brings together bigger capabilities such as Organizational Modeling and smaller changes that deserve a place in the test plan. For each area, I have included the practical check I would make before adoption. 
 First, the dates and availability 
 The main SAP SuccessFactors 2H 2026 Preview release became available on 12 October 2026 . . Its release hub currently shows 13 to 14 November in the annual calendar and 13 to 15 November in the 2H update section. Confirm your tenant’s exact production window using the release upgrade schedule available thru SAP's product release & roadmap hub. 
 There are also feature-specific dates and conditions: 
 Item Published availability Planning implication 
 Story page scope filters Preview: 20 October 2026. 
 Production: 16 November 2026. Schedule testing against these dates. 
 Effective-dated Time Valuation Restricted availability; valid from 13 November 2026. Requires an approved request and enablement. 
 WalkMe Learning Arc integration First integration step announced for Q4 2026. Confirm availability and prerequisites for your landscape. 
 1. Employee Central: Organizational Modeling is worth a closer look 
 This is one of my favourites in the release. 
 SAP introduces a workspace to simulate organisational changes, review the proposed structure and submit changes to Employee Central. Supported objects include Legal Entity, Business Unit, Division, Department, Cost Center and Position. 

 The solution runs on SAP BTP and SAP states that it is included in the Employee Central subscription at no additional cost. Adoption requires provisioning requests for Preview and Production, Position Management with position-to-job synchronisation, and access configured in both SuccessFactors RBP and SAP Cloud Identity Services. 
 My practical check: Start with one department move in Preview. Compare the proposed changes, resulting object records, Job Information and downstream integration output. Define who may publish changes and how the business will approve them. 
 2. People Profile: documents, printing and fewer repeated entries 
 A central place to find employee documents 
 The new Documents category brings supported employee attachments into the latest People Profile. Existing permissions govern which documents a user can access. In-system preview is available for supported file formats, with downloading still available. 

 Two details need attention: the category is enabled and available to all roles by default, while document access remains permission-controlled; and the initial scope excludes dependent documents and uncategorised attachments in MDF fields. 
 Uploading, renaming and deleting still take place in the originating application or profile section. Customers using a partner document workspace should review whether both experiences should be visible. 
 My practical check: Test with an employee, manager and HR role. Include someone outside the permitted target population. Verify both which categories are visible and which documents can actually be opened. 
 Print Profile deserves its own check 
 The 2H 2026 People Profile documentation adds printing and PDF export. Users can select the entire accessible profile or selected content, preview it and export it. The output follows viewing permissions, retains masking and reflects the selected effective date. SAP also states that administrators cannot deactivate the print option for all users. 

 My practical check: Include PDF output in permission testing. Check sensitive fields, masking and historical dates, then update guidance for anyone still being told that printing is unavailable in the latest profile. 
 Valid dependent values can stay in place 
 When a primary field changes, supported dependent fields are now checked before being cleared. A value that remains valid is retained. This applies to Edit and History Create/Correct operations in the latest People Profile. The enhancement is automatically enabled. 
 My practical check: Test a Business Unit change where the current Division remains valid, and another where it becomes invalid. Include the rules attached to those fields in the same regression test. 
 3. Business rules: easier maintenance and more useful performance controls 
 Variables can be edited after they are used 
 Used variables can now be edited within a business rule. Their data type must remain unchanged. SAP also improves warning visibility by highlighting variables that cause warnings. This is automatically enabled. 
 For me, this is exactly the kind of small enhancement that deserves attention. It makes a familiar maintenance task easier to handle. 
 My practical check: Update a variable in a representative rule in Preview, then test every branch that uses it. Include null values and boundary dates where relevant. 
 Performance rules gain more context 
 Performance Management rules gain support for section comments, text-length conditions and additional subject-user information. For example, a rule can require a section explanation when specified rating conditions are met. Text-length evaluation excludes rich-text HTML tags. 
 The latest form experience and Performance Management business rules must be enabled. Subject-user information is also available without Employee Central, but the field selection is smaller. SAP clarified that distinction in its 9 October revision. The enhancement is customer-configured. 
 My practical check: Agree one useful validation with the performance process owner, then test it through form routing. A minimum character count should support a meaningful explanation; it should not become the measure of feedback quality. 
 4. Time Management: effective dating could simplify policy changes 
 Effective-dated Time Valuation allows different configuration slices within a valuation. This can reduce the need to clone time recording profiles and update employee assignments for policy changes. 
 This feature has restricted availability. SAP requires request approval before enabling it through Upgrade Center. Valuation type and method cannot be changed when editing; slices cannot be made inactive. The Create Time Record valuation type does not support time slices. 
 There is also a calculation distinction: daily methods use the relevant day, while whole-sheet or period valuation uses the slice effective at the period end. 
 My practical check: If this fits your landscape, confirm eligibility first. Test a policy change inside a weekly period, including recalculation and payroll output. The result at the date boundary is more important than the appearance of the new configuration screen. 
 5. Recruiting and Onboarding: look at the specific process changes 
 Career Site Builder 
 Career Site Builder adds a Page Title component rendered as an H1 heading, limited to one per page. SmartRecruiters connection and Winston Chat settings move into a dedicated settings area. This is a customer-configured 2H enhancement. 
 My practical check: Review career-page heading structure and update administrator instructions for the settings location. Where applicable, retest the candidate journey through the connected ATS and chat experience. 
 For release tracking, keep the dates precise: the earlier SmartRecruiters mapping and prefill enhancements have a valid-from date of 15 June 2026 , even though their release entry also carries a 2H 2026 version tag. 
 Onboarding document traceability 
 For US Form I-9 processes, SAP adds attachment identifiers to the I9AuditTrail reporting schema for List A, B and C documents. These support tracing attachments to their I-9 records and identifying specific documents for targeted DMS purging. The same release item improves address mapping for E-Verify cases involving global assignments. It is automatically enabled. 

 My practical check: Test document-to-record traceability and the global-assignment address scenario with the onboarding team. Have the records owner review any purge procedure before operational use. 
 6. Succession: keep nominations aligned when someone takes the role 
 A new scheduled job can remove a successor from a position’s active nomination list when that person becomes its incumbent, and update the nomination history accordingly. 
 It requires MDF position-based nominations, Employee Central Position Management and the existing setting that removes a successor upon becoming incumbent. It is customer-configured. 
 Pay attention to the processing scope: the job handles changes effective on its execution date. 
 My practical check: Test a future-dated appointment on the day it becomes effective. Verify both the active nomination and its history, and agree how the support team will handle a missed run. 
 7. Story reports: let the reader choose the relevant scope 
 Scope filters can be placed on a story page so readers can adjust the reporting population at runtime. The relevant objects must first have scope filtering enabled in the query designer. Page-level selections take precedence over the query-level scope. 
 Runtime selections are not retained when saving the story or a bookmark, and switching from viewing to editing discards them. The enhancement is automatically enabled, with the separate Preview and Production dates shown above. 

 My practical check: Choose reports that currently differ mainly by population. Test whether one design can serve those use cases, and verify results with the intended manager and HR roles. Include the reset behaviour in user guidance. 
 8. Administration: make release decisions and transports easier to follow 
 Release Center 
 Release Center adds bulk actions, improved assignment filters, a status for items outside your interest, and downloads that include status and comments. These improvements are automatically enabled. 
 My practical check: Assign an owner and record the adoption decision for each relevant item. Recheck revised articles before closing the release assessment. 
 Configuration Transport Center 
 For MDF data-based configuration, external codes are now displayed alongside labels during configuration selection, in source and target bundle views, and in validation and import reports. This helps distinguish objects with identical labels. The change is automatically enabled. 
 My practical check: Include the external code in transport review evidence, especially where similar rule names exist across countries or processes. 
 9. AI for integrations: a clear support use case 
 AI-assisted integration insights bring on-demand analysis into Execution Manager for failed Integration Center runs. The feature analyses event logs and provides a root-cause explanation with suggested corrective actions. 

 It requires SAP AI Units, activation of Assisted Integration Insights, and the relevant administration, Execution Manager and AI-access permissions. This is a customer-configured feature. 
 My practical check: Evaluate it against a known failure in Preview. Compare its explanation with the logs, validate the proposed correction and rerun the integration. I would measure diagnosis time and recommendation quality before expanding usage. 
 10. Learning and Joule Assistants: plan against the delivery detail

items.title: calculate interest on loan less the full annuity (principal + interest) in SAP TRM
items.author: shady_elhefnawy
items.text:
Dear Experts., 
 In the annuity repayment method, SAP calculates the interest on the loan less the principal portion of the installment. We need the system to calculate the interest on the loan less the full annuity amount, that is, principal plus interest. 
 Example (product 55A, loan 1,000,000 EGP 10% act/360, quarterly installments paid at the start of each period, first installment 62,775.61): 
 - Current SAP calculation: interest base = 1,000,000 - 38,196.18 (principal only) = 961,803.82, interest 24,579.43 
 - Required calculation: interest base = 1,000,000 - 62,775.61 (principal + interest) = 937,224.39, interest 23,951.29 

 Please advise whether this can be done through Customizing or an enhancement, and what you recommend. 

 Best regards, 
 Shady Osama

items.title: One Click to a Clean Employee Record: Print and Export People Profile to PDF in 2H 2026
items.author: shaktibarath
items.text:
The screenshot workaround ends 
 From 13 November 2026, anyone who can view a latest People Profile can export it to a clean, dated PDF. It is switched on automatically and has no permission of its own. That makes it both a big productivity win and a governance item HR must review before go-live. 
 Today, when a talent committee, an auditor or an executive needs an employee summary, HR improvises. Someone takes screenshots of profile cards, pastes them into a slide or Word file, and hopes nothing changed since. The output is inconsistent, undated and hard to trust. 
 The new Print Profile action replaces that with a standard, as-of-dated document. The release note tags it "Info only". In my view, that undersells it: a feature that lets data leave the system deserves a deliberate decision. 
 What SAP shipped in 2H 2026 
 Print Profile sits in the Actions menu of the latest People Profile and exports Spotlight and Full Profile data to PDF. You choose the whole profile or specific categories and cards, then preview and remove individual cards before exporting. 

 What the PDF contains 
 Details 

 Timestamp 
 Print time, in the logged-in user's locale 

 As-of date 
 Matches the date selected on the Full Profile, so effective-dated data reflects that date 

 Header data 
 Everything visible in the Full Profile header and Profile Preview, except self-descriptions and matrix managers 

 Cards 
 Full details page where one exists, otherwise the summary card; original order kept, Documents always last 

 Empty fields 
 Always included 

 Status indicators 
 Pending Workflow and future-change notices appear; so do error messages 

 Attachments 
 Shown as file names only 

 Removed 
 Action buttons and card help 

 File name 
 [DisplayName] Profile [Date].pdf 

 Why it matters for HR 
 The as-of date is what makes this more than a print button. Every PDF states exactly which date the effective-dated data reflects, so the document can stand as a record. Four HR situations benefit right away. 
 Talent and succession reviews. Committees often include leaders who rarely log in. HR can prepare a consistent pack of candidate profiles, limited to the relevant categories, in minutes. 
 Audits and compliance checks. An auditor asks what an employee's job and contract data looked like on a given date. Set the Full Profile date, export, and the PDF carries both the as-of date and the print timestamp. 
 Employee relations and legal matters. Case files need a dated snapshot of the record at a point in time. A system-generated PDF is cleaner evidence than a screenshot. 
 Transfers, mergers and offboarding. When a record must move to another entity, or be retained for a period, HR has a standard format instead of ad-hoc extracts. 
 SAP positions it for talent managers, recruiters, compliance officers and executives who need profile data without direct system access. That last phrase is exactly why governance matters. 
 Governance: the part not to skip 
 Print appears for every user who can access the latest People Profile and view the data, with no separate permission to grant or withhold. In practice, your view permissions now also decide who can export profiles to a portable file. 
 SAP has built in sensible protections: 
 Data the user has no permission for is hidden in the PDF, as on screen. 
 Fields masked in the data model stay masked; unmasking in print is not supported. 
 The annualized salary chart is left out, and the amount field is always masked. 
 What the system cannot control is what happens to the file afterwards. A PDF can be emailed, saved to a personal drive or printed and left on a desk. For HR, that raises questions worth answering before 13 November: 
 Are our view permissions still right now that viewing also means exporting? Pay special attention to managers, matrix roles and broad "view all" HR groups. 
 Which categories hold sensitive data, such as dependents, national IDs, payment details or health-related leave, and are they masked or restricted? 
 Does our data retention and acceptable-use policy cover exported employee records? 
 Do works councils or privacy officers in any country need to be informed? 
 The annualized salary exclusion shows SAP thought about pay sensitivity. Your own sensitive custom fields need the same thought from you. 
 Rollout steps, watch-outs and tests 
 Because it switches on by itself, the work is a pre-release review rather than a configuration task. The steps and test ideas below are my suggestions. 
 Review view permissions in preview. Treat "can view" as "can export" and adjust roles that are broader than they need to be. 
 Check masking on sensitive fields. Confirm which fields are masked in the data model, because masking carries into the PDF. 
 Brief privacy and legal. Agree how exported profiles may be stored, shared and deleted. 
 Communicate to users. Tell HR, managers and executives what the feature is for, and what it is not for. 
 Build use-case templates. For talent reviews, define which categories to include so packs look the same every time. 

 Test 
 What to check 

 Manager vs HR admin export of the same employee 
 Each PDF shows only what that role can see on screen 

 Masked custom field 
 Stays masked in the PDF 

 Compensation category 
 Salary chart absent, amount masked 

 Past as-of date on Full Profile 
 PDF data and as-of date match that date 

 Record with a pending workflow 
 Pending notice appears, so readers know data may change 

 Documents category 
 Prints last, with attachment file names only 

 Long profile in different browsers 
 Layout and page breaks are readable 
 Closing thought 
 Print Profile solves a real, everyday HR problem: getting a trustworthy, dated employee record to people who are not in the system. Its as-of date and built-in masking make it far better than any screenshot. 
 But it arrives switched on, with no permission of its own. The HR teams that get the most from it will be the ones who spend an hour in preview checking who can view what. Do that, and you gain a clean record in one click without opening a new data risk. 
 Sources 
 SAP SuccessFactors What's New, 2H 2026 Platform release notes: "Print and Export People Profile to PDF" (ECT-268339, valid as of 13 November 2026). 
 SAP Help: Configuring the Latest People Profile (Printing People Profile)

items.title: Business AI in ABAP Cloud - Embedding AI with the ABAP AI SDK
items.author: fabianfellhauer
items.text:
Business AI in ABAP Cloud - Embedding AI with the ABAP AI SDK 
 Cheers ABAP Folks! 
 In my last blog post , we discussed the high-level strategy for implementing business AI capabilities in ABAP Cloud. We looked at the two pillars, Embedded AI in ABAP and Agentic AI via Joule , and when to use which approach. If you haven't read it yet, I'd recommend starting there for the bigger picture. 
 Today, we're going hands-on. This post dives into Embedded AI, the capabilities that run directly inside your ABAP application, powered by the ABAP AI SDK . We'll walk through the fundamentals, introduce the SDK, and then look at two concrete use cases using everyone's favorite business scenario: Trip & Expense Management . 
 Yes, trip & expense management. We all love it, don't we? Nothing brings more joy to a business traveler than filling out expense reports after a long trip. So, let's see how AI can take some of that joy... I mean burden ... away. 

 The Fundamentals: Connecting ABAP to AI 
 Before you write a single line of AI-related ABAP code, you need to get the plumbing right. All embedded AI scenarios in ABAP Cloud require a connection to SAP AI Core , specifically to the Generative AI Hub that provides access to Large Language Models (LLMs) hosted by hyperscalers. 
 This connection is established via Intelligent Scenario Lifecycle Management (ISLM) , a framework that allows you to manage and operate AI scenarios in a standardized, transportable way. Think of ISLM as the lifecycle backbone: it handles connectivity, model deployment, prompt management, and the runtime configuration that ties everything together. 
 Setting Up the Connection 
 The setup follows a straightforward pattern ( SAP Help, Set Up ABAP AI SDK powered by ISLM 
 Subscribe to SAP AI Core in your SAP BTP subaccount and enable the required service plan. 
 Create a service instance and service key for SAP AI Core in the BTP cockpit. 
 Establish connectivity between SAP AI Core and your ABAP system by creating a communication arrangement based on communication scenario SAP_COM_0A69 . 
 This is a customer-managed outbound integration, which means you own the connection setup. Once established, ISLM can create and activate model deployments, and the ABAP AI SDK can execute prompts against the deployed models. For a detailed step-by-step walkthrough, I recommend the tutorial Set Up SAP BTP and Integrate SAP AI Core with ISLM on SAP Developers. 
 The ABAP AI SDK, Your AI Toolbox 
 With the connection established, let's talk about the tool you'll actually use in your ABAP code: the ABAP AI SDK . It's a typed, ABAP-native reuse library that provides access to generative AI functionality via ISLM. It is available across the full ABAP Cloud landscape, covering: 
 SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition & On-Premise 
 SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition 
 SAP Business AI Platform, ABAP environment (Steampunk) 
 This means the same SDK, the same APIs, the same patterns, regardless of where your ABAP system runs. 
 What's in for me? 
 The ABAP AI SDK offers a set of APIs built around common LLM usage patterns: 
 Completion API – Send a prompt to an LLM and receive a generated text response. This is the core building block for most embedded AI scenarios. 
 Prompt Library API – Work with prompt templates predefined in ISLM, including parameterized prompts with runtime variable substitution. Very useful when you want to keep your prompts maintainable and out of your ABAP code. 
 Connectivity management – The SDK handles the connection to the Generative AI Hub transparently. You reference an intelligent scenario by name, and the SDK resolves the rest. 
 Exception handling – Typed ABAP exceptions, so you can integrate AI calls into your existing error handling patterns without reinventing the wheel. 
 The APIs are vendor-neutral, meaning the same ABAP code works regardless of which underlying LLM provider is configured in SAP AI Core. If your organization switches from one model to another, you change the configuration in ISLM, not your ABAP code. Your CTO changes their mind about the AI vendor? No problem, no code change required – ok, to be honest with you: The prompting might be polished most probably a little. 
 The Simplest Possible Call 
 To give you a feel for the developer experience, here's the simplest possible AI call using the Completion API ( SAP ABAP Cheat Sheets, Generative AI 😞 " Get a Completion API instance for your intelligent scenario
DATA(ai_api) = cl_aic_islm_compl_api_factory=>get( )->create_instance( 'Z_MY_SCENARIO' ).

" Execute a prompt and get the result
DATA(result) = ai_api->execute_for_string( `Classify this trip as customer-facing or internal.` ).

" Retrieve the generated text
DATA(completion) = result->get_completion( ). 
 Three lines of ABAP. That's it. The factory creates an instance tied to your intelligent scenario (which contains all the connection and model details), you execute a prompt, and you get back the LLM's response as a string. No HTTP client setup, no JSON parsing, no authentication handling. The SDK takes care of all of that. If you've ever tried calling a REST API from ABAP the "old-fashioned way", you'll know exactly how much boilerplate this saves you. 
 Of course, real-world scenarios are a bit more involved. You'll use prompt templates with parameters, handle exceptions, and integrate the result into your business logic. But the fundamental pattern stays the same. 
 Orchestration Capabilities 
 For enterprise-grade AI scenarios, the ABAP AI SDK also supports orchestration through the SAP AI Core Orchestration Service . This adds capabilities that are critical for production use: 
 Data Masking – Automatically redact sensitive information (personal data, financial details) before it reaches the LLM. Essential for data protection and GDPR compliance, and something your compliance team will thank you for. 
 Document Grounding – Enrich your prompts with business-relevant context from documents, reducing hallucinations and improving response accuracy. Because an LLM that confidently makes things up is entertaining at dinner parties, but not in your ERP system. 
 Content Filtering – Ensure that LLM responses are safe, appropriate, and compliant with your organisation's policies. 
 These capabilities are configured at the orchestration level, so you don't need to implement masking or filtering logic yourself in ABAP. It's handled for you. 

 Let’s get our hands dirty: Trip & Expense Management 
 For the rest of this blog post, we'll use a Trip & Expense Management application as our running example. Picture a RAP-based Fiori application where employees create travel requests, and after the trip, submit expense reports. 
 We'll tackle two concrete use cases: 
 Data Prediction with Fiori Input Assistance : Automatically categorizing a trip as "customer-facing" or "internal" based on the trip description. 
 Data Extraction from files : Extracting structured data (payment amounts, categories, etc.) from uploaded receipt documents. 
 Both are real-world scenarios that demonstrate different facets of the ABAP AI SDK. And both address the same fundamental truth: nobody enjoys filling out forms manually when a machine could do it better and faster. Let's start. 

 Use Case 1: Trip Categorization with RAP Recommendations 
 The Problem 
 When an employee creates a travel request, they need to fill out several fields: destination, purpose, cost center, and importantly, trip category (e.g. "customer-facing" or "internal"). This categorization drives downstream processes like approval workflows, budget allocation, and reporting. Today, users pick the category manually. They might get it wrong, or they pick whatever option is closest to the mouse cursor. What if the system could propose the right category automatically , based on the trip description? 
 The Solution: Fiori Input Assistance 
 This is exactly what Fiori Input Assistance implemented with RAP recommendations is designed for. RAP recommendations are a built-in input assistance feature in the ABAP RESTful Application Programming Model (RAP) that proposes field values for input fields on an SAP Fiori UI ( SAP Help, Defining RAP Recommendations ). Available since SAP BTP ABAP Environment 2602 and SAP S/4HANA Cloud 2602 , RAP Recommendations can be implemented using either deterministic rules or generative AI , and you can even mix both approaches in the same application. The key principles of RAP recommendations: 
 They are exposed in SAP Fiori as a recommendation pattern of type input assistance, meaning the user sees suggested values directly in the input field. 
 They are built on top of a value help, so you need an existing value help for the target field. 
 They are triggered by side effects: when the user changes a source field (e.g. trip description), the recommendation function runs and proposes values for the target field (e.g. trip category). 
 They integrate seamlessly with the RAP programming model. No custom UI development required. Zero. Nada. 
 Figure 1: Fiori Input Assistance implemented with RAP recommendations 
 How It Works: The Architecture 
 The implementation involves three layers: 
 Behavior Definition – Declare which fields receive recommendations and define the recommendation function. 
 Behavior Implementation – Implement the recommendation logic in the behavior pool, using the ABAP AI SDK to call an LLM for intelligent categorization. 
 Projection Behavior Definition – Expose the recommendations in the projection layer for the Fiori UI. 
 If you've built a RAP Business Object before, this will feel very familiar. It's the same layered pattern, just with AI sprinkled on top. 
 Step 1: Define Recommendations in the Behavior Definition 
 In your behavior definition, you mark the target field as relevant for recommendations, declare a recommendation function and define a side effect on which the recommendation function should be triggered. This tells the RAP framework: whenever the user changes the “ title ” field, execute function GetRecommendedValuesFunction and propose values for attribute “ type ”. The user types "Customer workshop in Berlin" and the system immediately suggests "Customer-facing". It almost feels like the system is reading the user's mind, except it's reading their input field. define behavior for ZR_AITRIP alias Trip
{
 //Define for which fields an recommendation output is generated
 field ( recommendations ) Type;

 //Define the recommendation function itself
 recommendation function GetRecommendedValuesFunction;

 //Define the trigger (e.g. other context field)
 side effects
 {
 recommendation function GetRecommendedValuesFunction 
 executed on field Title;
 }
} 
 Step 2: Implement the Recommendation Logic 
 In the behavior pool, you implement the recommendation function. This is where the ABAP AI SDK comes in. You use the completion API to ask an LLM to categorize the trip based on the available context: 
 Read the current entity data (description, destination, etc.) 
 Build a prompt with the trip context, based on your system's master data 
 Call the ABAP AI SDK Completion API 
 Parse the LLM response 
 Return the recommended value(s) with scores 
 The recommendation function returns a list of proposed values, each with a score and a flag indicating whether it's the suggested (top-ranked) value. The Fiori UI renders these as input assistance. The user can accept, modify, or override the suggestion. The AI proposes, the human decides. As it should be.

items.title: SAP SuccessFactors Role-Based Permissions — Designing Permission Roles Leading Practice for EC Core
items.author: dayna_carnino
items.text:
The SAP SuccessFactors 2H 2026 release introduces an updated reference for Designing Permission Roles , providing 
 administrators and implementation consultants with a structured foundation for role design discussions and initial system 
 configuration. The initial design focuses on the most common permission roles used across the SAP SuccessFactors Employee 
 Central Core business scenario, covering each role's typical scope, purpose, and baseline permissions. This post walks through 
 the key attributes that shape role design and the common roles that serve as a starting point for building a secure, scalable, and 
 well-governed permission model. 

 What This Reference Covers 
 The Designing Permission Roles documentation serves as a practical starting point for role design discussions and initial system 
 configuration. It describes the most common roles used across SAP SuccessFactors implementations — including their typical 
 scope, purpose, and the permissions they generally include. Administrators and consultants can use it alongside SAP Best Practices 
 for HCM to accelerate and standardize the design process. 
 Role Design Attributes 
 No two implementations are identical. SAP SuccessFactors role design is shaped by a combination of factors that must be 
 evaluated before configuration begins: 
 Company size and organizational structure — Larger organizations typically require more granular roles to 
 reflect regional or departmental differences in data visibility and access 
 Modules purchased — Only modules included in the customer's subscription require permission configuration; 
 scope drives role count 
 Business scenarios — Different processes within a single module may require separate roles or distinct permission sets 
 Country-specific requirements — Data privacy laws and local HR practices may require country-specific role variants to 
 remain compliant 
 Company culture — Organizational norms — such as whether employees or managers initiate performance forms — 
 directly affect which roles need which permissions 
 To document and organize roles consistently, each role should be defined using the following attributes: 
 Attribute Description Example 
 Module The SAP SuccessFactors module the role applies to Employee Central 
 Business Scenario The functional area or process within the module Employee Central Core 
 Permission Role Name The name assigned to the role in the system Super Admin 
 Role Description Plain-language description of the role's purpose and scope Provides full administrative access to all 
 Employee Central configuration 
 Permission Category The category of a group of permissions in Manage Permission Roles General User Permission 
 Permission The name of a permission in Manage Permission Roles Proxy Rights 
 Note: In larger organizations, a single role may be split into multiple region- or country-specific roles. For example, instead 
 of one Manager role, a company may use separate Manager roles per region where different data visibility rules apply. 
 Common Permission Roles 
 The following roles appear across most SAP SuccessFactors implementations and serve as a baseline starting point for role design: 
 Permission Role Role Description 
 HRBP Acts as a strategic advisor to the business on HR-related matters 
 HR Administrator 
 Maintains employee master data and organizational assignments; initiates 
 and monitors data replication; maintains and approves time off 
 Manager on Direct Reports Receives notifications and views apprenticeship plans for direct reports 
 Employee on Self Accesses personal data and self-service capabilities 
 Super Admin Holds the highest level of system access across all modules and configurations 
 Note: The permissions above reflect common baseline configuration for the Employee Central Core business 
 scenario only. For country-specific fields — including Global Information, Job Information, and Pay Components — 
 consult the relevant country-level Best Practice files. For other Employee Central scenarios, refer to 
 SAP Best Practices for SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central . 
 What You Should Learn 
 Role design is not one-size-fits-all — Company size, modules purchased, business scenarios, 
 country-specific requirements, and company culture all directly influence how permission roles are structured 
 Document every role consistently — Using defined attributes (module, business scenario, role name, description, permission 
 category, and permission) ensures roles are organized, auditable, and easier to maintain over time 
 Start with the common baseline roles — HRBP, HR Administrator, Manager on Direct Reports, Employee on Self, and 
 Super Admin provide the foundation for most Employee Central Core implementations 
 Country-specific fields require additional steps — Global Information, Job Information, and Pay Components must be 
 configured using the relevant country-level Best Practice files — the baseline roles do not cover these automatically 
 Large organizations may need role variants — A single role such as Manager may need to be split into region or 
 country-specific versions where different data visibility rules apply 
 This reference covers Employee Central Core only — For other Employee Central business scenarios, consult 
 SAP Best Practices for SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central for the appropriate role and permission guidance 
 Conclusion 
 Designing permission roles thoughtfully — accounting for organizational structure, module scope, business scenarios, and 
 country-specific requirements — is essential to building a secure and maintainable SAP SuccessFactors implementation. 
 The common roles covered here provide a consistent baseline, but each implementation will require adjustments based on the 
 factors unique to that organization. For detailed permission descriptions and full role mapping guidance, refer to the 
 SAP Help documentation: Implementing Role-Based Permissions — Designing Permission Roles .

items.title: When I ask Joule something, what actually happens behind the scenes?
items.author: GouthamiR
items.text:
At first glance it may feel like you are simply chatting with an AI assistant. In reality there is an intelligent orchestration layer working behind the scenes to ensure every response is accurate, secure and connected to your business systems. Let's break it down. 
 Step 1: Everything starts with the user - Every interaction begins with a person. There are two ways a user can interact with AI: 
 Through Joule by asking a question (for example, "Who hasn't completed their performance review?") 
 Directly inside SAP SuccessFactors (HCM) by clicking an action, such as approving leave or updating employee information. Both paths eventually lead to the same AI engine. 
 Step 2: Joule or HCM sends the request to the Agent Runtime - The Agent Runtime acts like the brain or orchestrator. Instead of immediately generating an answer, it first plans the best way to fulfil the request. 
 Its job is to understand the request and decide: What information is needed?, Which systems should be contacted?, Which tools should be used?, Is the user authorized to perform this action? 
 Step 3: Agent Configuration decides how the request should be handled - Inside the Agent Runtime are three important components. 
 Agent Config - This is the AI's instruction manual. It defines: which agent should respond, what workflow to follow and which business rules apply. 
 A2A Client (Agent-to-Agent) - Sometimes one AI agent cannot complete the task alone. t may need help from another specialized agent. It defines: one agent understands HR policies, another specializes in recruiting and another handles payroll. 
 MCP Client - The MCP Client connects AI with enterprise systems. Instead of creating separate integrations for every application MCP provides one standard way to communicate with: SAP applications, databases, APIs, documents, custom enterprise systems 
 Step 4: Selecting the right tools - Once the runtime understands the request, it chooses the most suitable tool. The user never needs to choose these tools manually. Joule automatically selects the best one. 
 It might use: Calculator, Web Search, SAP Joule Functions, Custom enterprise applications, MCP-connected enterprise tools 
 Step 5: Large Language Models (LLM) do the reasoning - Once all the required information is collected, everything is sent to the Large Language Model (LLM). This is where AI actually thinks to generate an intelligent response. 
 The LLM combines: your question, enterprise data, tool outputs, business context, 
 Step 6: Agent Services keep everything secure - While all of this happens, another layer called Agent Services continuously monitors the process. It provides: 
 Guardrails – ensures AI follows company policies. 
 Metering – tracks resource usage. 
 Tracing – records what happened during each request. 
 Benchmarking – measures performance and quality. 
 Extensibility – allows organizations to add new capabilities in the future. 
 This architecture shows that Joule is much more than a chatbot. It acts as an intelligent coordinator that understands your request, connects to the right enterprise systems, collaborates with specialized AI agents, uses the appropriate tools, reasons with Large Language Models and delivers secure, governed and business-aware responses all within a unified AI framework.

items.title: SAP Business Data Cloud: CSVファイルからカスタムデータプロダクトの作成
items.author: yuiyoshikawa
items.text:
はじめに 
 SAP Business Data Cloud（BDC）では、お客様独自のデータをカスタムデータプロダクトとして定義・公開することができます。 
 カスタムデータプロダクトの作成方法については、以下ブログで詳しく解説されています。 
 SAP Business Data Cloud: カスタムデータプロダクトの作成 
 上記ブログでは、SAP S/4HANAからの複製フローを使ってデータをオブジェクトストア（SAP HDLFスペース）に取り込む方法が紹介されています。一方で、本ブログでは、CSVファイルをSAP Datasphereにアップロードするというよりシンプルな方法で、カスタムデータプロダクトの作成する手順をご紹介します。SAP Business Data Cloud Connectを活用したPoCや動作確認、学習目的でご活用いただくことを目的としています。 
 全体の流れ 
 カスタムデータプロダクトはオブジェクトストア（SAP HDLFスペース）に物理的に保持する必要があります。一方で、CSVファイルは直接オブジェクトストアにアップロードすることができない仕様となっているため、ワークアラウンドとして以下のフローでCSVファイルからカスタムデータプロダクトを作成します。 

 以下の手順を始める前に、オブジェクトストア（SAP HDLFスペース）が作成済みである必要があります。作成手順は SAP Business Data Cloud: オブジェクトストア 入門編 を参照してください。 
 手順 
 ① SAP HANA DBスペースにローカルテーブルを作成（CSVファイルをアップロード） 
 HANAスペースのデータビルダーより「CSVファイルからローカルテーブルを作成」を使って、CSVファイルをアップロードします。アップロードが完了すると、CSVの内容がローカルテーブルとして作成されます。 
 ② SAP HANA DBスペースのローカルテーブルをSAP HDLFスペースに共有 
 カスタムデータプロダクトはオブジェクトストア（SAP HDLFスペース）に物理的に保持する必要があります。SAP HANAスペースから、①で作成したローカルテーブルをSAP HDLFスペースに共有設定します。 
 2.1. SAP HANAスペースにて対象のローカルテーブルを選択し、共有ボタンをクリックします。ポップアップで共有先となるSAP HDLFスペースを選択します。 

 ③ SAP HDLFスペースにて変換フローでローカルテーブル(ファイル)に書き出す 
 SAP HDLFスペースを開き、共有されたテーブルが表示されていることを確認します。その後、変換フローを作成し、共有テーブルをソースとして、ローカルテーブル（ファイル）に書き出します。 
 3.1. データビルダをクリックし、SAP HDLFスペースを開きます。 

 3.2. ローカルテーブルが共有されていることを確認します。新規変換フローをクリックします。 

 3.3. 左の一覧より対象のローカルテーブルをSourceとしてドラッグ＆ドロップします。 

 3.4. targetをクリックし、右側のプロパティで「新規ターゲットテーブルの作成」をクリックします。 

 3.5. 書き出すローカルテーブル（ファイル）に名前をつけ、左上で、保存、デプロイ、実行をします。 

 ④ データ共有コックピットでデータプロダクトを定義して公開 
 SAP Business Data Cloud: カスタムデータプロダクトの作成 の「カスタムデータプロダクトの定義」の章をご覧ください。 
 まとめ 

 CSVアップロードを使った方法は、カスタムデータプロダクトの仕組みを素早く体験するのに最適です。全体のフローを理解したうえで、本番運用では こちらのブログ の複製フローを使った方法に移行することをお勧めします。

deep_dives.title: Calling an LLM from ABAP Cloud with the ABAP AI SDK
deep_dives.explanation:
The post describes the ABAP AI SDK as a thin layer over ISLM (Intelligent Scenario Lifecycle Management), which manages lifecycle, connectivity, deployment and prompts. ISLM connects to the Generative AI Hub in SAP AI Core, so no hand-written HTTP or JSON is needed.

Prerequisites come first: subscribe to SAP AI Core, create a service instance and service key, and create a communication arrangement for scenario `SAP_COM_0A69` (customer-managed outbound). Then an ISLM scenario, for example `Z_MY_SCENARIO`, must exist.

The call has three steps: `cl_aic_islm_compl_api_factory=>get( )->create_instance( 'Z_MY_SCENARIO' )` returns the API object, `execute_for_string( ... )` sends the prompt, and `get_completion( )` on the result returns the text. The excerpt does not show full signatures, so check them in ADT.

The Prompt Library API uses ISLM-managed prompt templates with parameters, which moves prompt text out of code. Orchestration through the SAP AI Core Orchestration Service adds data masking and document grounding. The post says the SDK is available in S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition/On-Premise, Public Edition and the ABAP environment; the post's vendor-neutrality claim should be tested in a real system.

deep_dives.title: Finding the source of a computed screen value
deep_dives.explanation:
The WB2R_SV post shows that a number on screen need not be stored in any table. Here the Net Amount is held in a structure that the settlement logic fills at runtime, so a table search finds nothing.

The approach described is to start at the list and follow the data to the method that populates the structure. In practice this means debugging from the UI, setting breakpoints at the output, and using where-used on the structure. The excerpt does not name the specific tools used, so these are general techniques.

For a Fiori Elements report this matters: a CDS view over tables cannot reproduce the value unless the calculation is reproduced or the logic is called. The author's three pre-report questions are not in the excerpt, so read the full post for them.

deep_dives.title: Why a published custom field is not exposed in a standard Public Cloud app
deep_dives.explanation:
The question describes field YY1_ContractEngineer (Text, 12) published on business context MM_PURDOC_HEADER. The mass-change views C_PURCNTRLCONTRMASSUPDT, C_PURCNTRLCONTITMMASSUPDT and C_PURCNTRLCONTRHIERMASSUPDT are enabled, yet the field is not selectable in Mass Changes to Purchase Contracts.

The post suggests that publication and exposure are separate steps. A field must be in the app's relevant CDS views and be offered by the app's own field configuration. The asker lists possible causes: business context fit for central versus local contracts, type or length limits, activation or refresh, and authorisations. No answer is given.

A practical check is to confirm the field appears in the Custom Fields app's User Interfaces tab for the right app, then check whether the mass-change view lists it as an extension element. Treat this as a diagnostic plan, not a confirmed fix.

interview_questions.question: What do you need in place before an ABAP Cloud program can call an LLM through the ABAP AI SDK?
interview_questions.answer: The SDK reaches the Generative AI Hub in SAP AI Core through ISLM. First, subscribe to SAP AI Core, create a service instance and a service key. Next, create a communication arrangement for scenario SAP_COM_0A69, which is customer-managed outbound. Then define an ISLM scenario. In code, cl_aic_islm_compl_api_factory=>get( )->create_instance( ) returns the completion API, execute_for_string sends the prompt and get_completion( ) reads the result. Because the setup spans BTP and the ABAP system, connectivity failures are the usual blocker, so error handling should be added around the call.

interview_questions.question: A user asks for a Fiori Elements report on a screen value for which you find no table. How do you proceed?
interview_questions.answer: I would not assume the value is stored. Many values are computed at runtime and held in structures filled by the application logic, as in the WB2R_SV Net Amount case. I would debug from the UI, find the structure behind the field, and use where-used to locate the method that fills it. Then I decide whether to reuse that logic, reproduce the calculation in a CDS view, or persist results. I would also confirm the calculation depends on context, such as settlement runs, before committing to a report. Only then do I estimate and promise the delivery.

interview_questions.question: In S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition a published custom field does not appear in a standard mass-change app. How would you analyse it?
interview_questions.answer: Publishing a field makes it available in the business context, but an app only shows it if its relevant CDS views and field configuration expose it. I would check the Custom Fields app, in particular the User Interfaces tab and the status. I would then check that the mass-change views (here for contracts C_PURCNTRLCONTRMASSUPDT and related) include the extension. I would also test the business context for central versus local contracts, and field type and length restrictions. Finally I would check activation and authorisation roles. The source question has no confirmed answer, so I would confirm with SAP documentation or a support incident.
